card.line: Bethsaida was a fishing town by the Sea of Galilee, home to Philip, Andrew, and Peter, where Jesus healed a blind man and which He warned for not repenting.

moments.title: Jesus Withdraws to Bethsaida
moments.text: After the apostles returned and reported what they had done, Jesus took them away privately to a town called Bethsaida. The crowds followed, and He welcomed them, taught them, and healed those who needed it.

moments.title: Disciples Sent Ahead
moments.text: After five thousand men had eaten the loaves, Jesus made His disciples get into the boat and go on ahead of Him to Bethsaida. He dismissed the crowd and went up on the mountain to pray.

moments.title: A Blind Man Healed
moments.text: At Bethsaida, people begged Jesus to touch a blind man, and He led him out of the village. After Jesus placed His hands on the man's eyes a second time, the man could see everything clearly.

moments.title: Home of Philip, Andrew, and Peter
moments.text: John tells us that Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter. Jesus had told Philip, "Follow Me."

moments.title: Woe to Bethsaida
moments.text: Jesus spoke sharp words to Bethsaida because it saw His miracles and did not repent. He said Tyre and Sidon would have repented long ago if they had seen them.
